StuffItem.description: Something kept in My Stuff. Docs and code carry their opening (excerpt); links their url; apps their entry, file count and whether they run

allowed.description: What a pane may use now: tasks:write only while its code is what you allowed

published.description: Its public link on a wisp Grid, and the version (rev) that went up

changed.description: Its code moved since you allowed tasks:write

risky.description: What its code does that wisp can’t hold back

Hold.description: Refused: it would take the account’s usage window past the Ask near the limit line (Settings → Usage)

to.description: Where it would likely end up, low and high (0..1)

hint.description: The last 4 characters of the key

hasKey.description: opencode only: signed in to a provider or has an API key in the environment (false: its free models alone)

setup.description: Only while not found: how to get it on that OS

budget.description: How much of each account’s usage windows is gone, as its CLI last reported (Claude, Codex). hitAt: when it runs out at this pace, if before the reset. where: the tasks that used most of the longest window, and where.subagents: its share by subagent type ({ type, calls, model, output, used, instead })

overage.description: Past your plan: runs on this account billed beyond the plan in the last 7 days (kind: extra = Claude extra usage, credits = Codex credits, api = an API key, profile = a Claude Console sign-in). Each such turn also has turn.overage { kind, at }

notices.description: Window changes (defaults.windowNotice, on unless off): a window that appeared (new), went (gone), changed length (length: wasMs) or moved its reset off its schedule (reset: wasResetsAt), until dismissed

compare.description: Tokens per turn by account, only with several accounts: per model this harness ran on two or more accounts in the last 7 days, each account’s median finished turn (output and input tokens; input counts cache reads and writes) and the share it read from the cache, once each account shown has 5 turns on that model. A diagnostic: wisp never picks an account from it

missing.description: Tools another account in this row had on its latest turn and this one did not (Claude Code’s init tool list, wisp’s own MCP tools left out)

pinnedAt.description: Harness watch: when wisp pinned its program (path, size, sha256, version)

changed.description: Harness watch: its program is not the pinned one. kind: update (version up, same install folder) or warn

from.description: The tool they came from: Conductor

chat.description: A Claude conversation was found for this folder, and resumes on the next message

detached.description: Worktrees here with no branch: counted, not offered

confirmLimit.description: The user agreed to go ahead although it would take the account’s usage window past their Ask near the limit line (see the 409 `hold`)

cwd.description: Project folder (absolute; ~ allowed). Default: the server’s cwd

also.description: More folders the same task works in (absolute; ~ allowed). The agent gets each; git repos get their own worktree, and Ship it opens a PR in each

scratch.description: No project folder: run in an empty scratch directory (no worktree). Overrides cwd

kind.description: pane: Make a pane. The agent builds an app for My Stuff and pins it (the same empty folder, Edits mode, this computer). spell: Cast a spell. The agent writes a spell that changes wisp (an empty scratch folder, Edits mode, this computer); its report ends with a spell block to keep

agent.description: auto: wisp picks the harness and model from what worked before; model is then the goal (cheap, balanced, best)

important.description: With agent auto: no exploring, take the pick with the best record

autoPin.description: With agent auto: the pick a preview showed (an arm key, 'claude:opus:high'); it runs if it still can

autoOverride.description: With a harness you picked: the pick Auto previewed instead, so it learns from the change

effort.description: Thinking level: low, medium, high, xhigh, max (per harness)

account.description: Which of the harness’s accounts to run on (`/agents/{aid}/accounts`); none: your last pick (skipping one already at its usage limit)

worktree.description: Run in a fresh git worktree + branch. Default: on in git repos (Settings), off in plan mode

use.description: When the lead should pick this one

count.description: Identical copies that take tasks in parallel (name#1, name#2, …); 12 in all

machine.description: Where it runs: empty (with the lead), `here` (this computer), a machine id, or `sandbox` (a box of its own on your wisp Grid, kept for the task; Claude Code only). One on another place works on a copy of the lead’s work there; its changes come back as a patch

subagents.description: A team the lead can delegate to through the injected `delegate` tool. Each runs as a child session in the lead’s folder

preset.description: Id of a saved team (`/teams`), used when `subagents` is absent

crew.description: A crew member, on their own harness

judges.description: Each checks the work on its own; [] clears them

vote.description: How many judges must say met (default majority). Can’t be done takes a majority

goal.description: Keep going until this holds: after each turn wisp checks it and sends the task back with what is missing. A prompt that is just `/goal <condition>` does the same

subagentModel.description: Claude Code only (400 on anything else): the model this task’s subagents run on, over defaults.subagentModel. '' is the task’s own model; left out, the setting

skills.description: Claude Code only (400 on anything else): run without its skills and slash commands. Plugins, agents and CLAUDE.md stay. Left out, they’re on

trial.description: Try it two ways: these runs compare one setup with one change, and each gets session.trial. Needs compare, a harness you picked (not Auto), a mode other than plan, and a project with a worktree per run (not worktree: false or scratch): 400 otherwise

account.description: Which of the harness’s accounts this run uses; none = your last pick

subagentModel.description: As at the top level, for this run

skills.description: As at the top level, for this run

compare.description: Also run the same task on these, each in its own worktree

conflict.description: GitHub cannot merge it into its base: merge conflicts

use.description: What the lead should use it for

machine.description: Empty (with the lead), `here` or a machine id

cwd.description: Project path, or empty for any project

name.description: Up to 24 characters; @Name in a prompt reaches them

avatar.description: An emoji; empty shows the initial

brief.description: Their standing job, in every job’s prompt

cwd.description: The folder their jobs run in (on their machine, if they have one); empty = no project

machine.description: A machine id: their jobs run there as its tasks; their memory, schedule and queue stay here. Empty = this computer

sandbox.description: Their jobs run in a box on your wisp Grid with their project as it is here: `job` a fresh one per job (deleted with the job), `own` one kept for them (their installs stay; deleted with them). Clears machine. Claude Code or auto only

cron.description: When they check in, in words ("8am every weekday") or 5-field cron, local time; stored as cron. Empty = only when asked

parallel.description: Jobs at once; more wait in the queue

paused.description: No check-ins, triggers or delegations start; your own jobs still do

notebook.description: Their memory, kept by them (a hidden crew block ends each job) and editable by you

kit.description: Their skills and instructions files. rules (an AGENTS.md) are in every job’s prompt; a skill’s name and description are, and the job reads its SKILL.md when it fits. on: false keeps one without using it

path.description: A skill’s folder on this computer (its scripts and references)

log.description: One line per finished job, newest first

wakeAt.description: A check-in they asked for; null clears it

offers.description: Skills and instructions files their jobs proposed for their kit (newest first): { id, job, at, files, state: open | taken | dismissed, names }. PATCH offers: [{ id, state, names }] settles them (send the kit with the files you add)

on.description: What else starts their jobs: the kinds of the triggers that are on and send them work. Sent (finished, done, ci), it makes or removes those triggers

spell.description: A member a spell brought: { id, key, name, def }. The spell owns def (name, role, avatar, brief, schedule, on, mode, kit, delegates); changing those is refused (409) until POST /crew/{cid}/detach

changed.description: Their spell changed what they do (from: the old definition, null for a member it just added): they are paused, and resume only with accept: true

accept.description: PATCH with paused: false: you saw what their spell changed

crew.description: A crew member id: the work goes to them as a job (cwd may then be empty for a schedule or a task watcher)

kind.description: finished: a task finished a turn; done: a task was marked done; webhook, slack, linear: its URL (POST /hooks/{token}) was called

cwd.description: finished/done: only tasks in this project; empty = the crew member’s project, or any

prompt.description: Template; ci gets {id} {name} {branch} {sha} {url}, issues get {number} {title} {body} {url} {author}, finished/done get {id} {title} {summary} {branch} {cwd}; webhook gets {{body.a.b}} {{text}}, slack {{text}} {{user}} {{channel}}, linear {{title}} {{url}} {{description}} {{identifier}}

recipeId.description: Run this recipe instead of prompt

cron.description: schedule: when, in words ("every monday") or 5-field cron, local time; stored as cron

branch.description: ci: only failures on this branch

label.description: issues: the label to watch; linear: only issues with this label (empty: any)

token.description: webhook/slack/linear: the secret part of its URL, /api/hooks/{token}

regenerate.description: A new token: the old URL stops working

secret.description: webhook: signs deliveries (HMAC sha256 of the body, optional); slack: the app’s signing secret; linear: the webhook’s signing secret. Never sent back (hasSecret); left out it stays, null clears it

header.description: webhook: the header carrying the signature (default X-Hub-Signature-256), hex or sha256=hex

channel.description: slack: the channel id (C0123456789) whose mentions and messages start tasks

keyword.description: slack: only messages with this word

users.description: slack: the member IDs who may start it (in Slack: their profile → ⋯ → Copy member ID). A new or edited trigger needs at least one

open.description: slack: saved before people had to be named, so anyone in the channel can start it. Pausing it or a new URL still work; any other edit needs users

compactOffer.description: Compact now is offered: tokens, the USD estimates compact and cold (null on a model wisp has no price for), and until (ms): when the offer ends

preview.description: The hero summary of the latest turn

live.description: One-line status while running, or the pending question

queueHeld.description: A Stop held the queued follow-ups: none goes out until you send something or Send now

branch.description: Worktree branch, if it has one

foreign.description: 'conductor': a worktree it was brought in on, which wisp never removes; '' otherwise

shipping.description: { step: start | commit | push | pr, update } while Ship it runs

review.description: Review by another harness of the PR's head (defaults.review): { status: running | done | failed | held, head, current (of the PR's head now), by: { agent, model }, summary, findings: [{ severity: high | medium | low, file, line, text }], tests: { verdict, command, passed, failed }, coverage: how much of the diff the reviewer was given, when it was computed: { files, seen (files whole), chars, seenChars, cut: [paths only partly in it], missing: [paths not in it], more (names dropped past 50 between cut and missing, left out when 0) }; seen < files is a partial review, and with no findings its summary is wisp's own, why }

conflictFix.description: { step: fixing | pushing | done | failed, why } while wisp fixes the PR's merge conflicts: after Fix conflicts, or on its own with defaults.fixConflicts: 'on'

overlaps.description: Other open tasks in the same repo that change the same files: [{ id, title, files, more, conflicts }]. conflicts lists the files merging both would leave conflicted ([] if they merge cleanly, null if git is older than 2.38). Absent when there are none.

groupId.description: Shared by sessions launched together with compare

origin.description: { kind: recipe | trigger, id, name } when not launched by hand

keepWorktree.description: The worktree cleanup leaves this task’s folder alone (PATCH keepWorktree)

subagentModel.description: This task’s own subagent model, when it has one ('': the task’s model), over defaults.subagentModel

skills.description: Claude Code runs without its skills and slash commands, when set

values.description: One per run, in run order

trial.description: Try it two ways, on the full task (GET /sessions/{id}), not in lists: what differed between its runs

lean.description: This task’s own lean runs choice (PATCH lean), when it has one

Btw.description: A side question (/btw). It sits on turns[].btw of the turn it was asked during; GET the session or wait for its turn event to see the answer

forked.description: Answered on a copy of the agent’s conversation (else from wisp’s record of the task)
